I'll read the script first so I know how to run it under the profiler.
The script has two candidates: `isPrime` (trial division) inside `countPrimes`, and `dedupe` (`Array.includes` on a growing array). Next I'll profile it.
The profiler couldn't write its output inside the sandbox. I'll retry with Node's built-in `--cpu-prof` writing to a scratch directory outside the repo.
`isPrime` is the slowest function, taking about 78% of the self time (about 211 ms in this run). `dedupe` is second at about 10%.

The volt profiler couldn't write its output in this sandbox (EPERM), so I profiled with Node's `--cpu-prof` into `/tmp/slow-prof` instead. No files in the repo were changed.

`isPrime` is trial division up to `n`, so it is O(n) per number and dominates the 60,000-number loop in `countPrimes`. The main fix would be a sieve or checking divisors only up to √n. `dedupe` is quadratic because `out.includes` scans the array on every item.
